gap: No result ChatGPT got states that losing one AeroClip 2 earbud costs $79.99 to replace through Soundcore's US store, which is 47% of a new $169.99 set and $40.01 more than a whole new C50i set at $39.98. Calls cost $8.50 per rated call-hour on the AeroClip 2 and $2.22 on the C50i, and the AeroClip 2 gets only 0.5 h more talk time per charge.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited or ranked: soundcore.com's AeroClip 2 and C50i product pages, the clip-on collection page, Soundcore's AeroClip vs AeroClip 2 blog, our own dealectric.com/soundcore-aeroclip-2-vs-c50i, and Expert Reviews' AeroClip 2 review by Andy White (2026-10-30). The TechRadar page would not load, and B&H returned 403. None of these pages gives a replacement-earbud price, and none puts the two call-time ratings (5 h/20 h vs 4.5 h/18 h) side by side. The AeroClip 2 product page doesn't list call time at all; it appears only in the blog's comparison table. All three ChatGPT answers compare music hours (8/32 vs 7/28) only. Our current page also has no cost per hour and no parts price. The raw inputs are on Soundcore pages, but none of them does this arithmetic, so it isn't a 3. It also doesn't overturn the call-quality pick, which still rests on the Guinness G-MOS certification and Expert Reviews calling the call quality 'exceptional'.
decides: It backs the C50i for running and gym use, where a clip-on bud is more likely to get knocked off. A lost C50i means buying a whole new set for $39.98, while a lost AeroClip 2 bud costs $79.99. It also shows that the AeroClip 2's extra price buys mic quality, not much battery. On a call-heavy day it gets 5 h per charge against 4.5 h, so both need the case after about one 4.5–5 h stretch of calls. The extra $130 should rest on call clarity alone.
